reply.failure_summary: After Place order, the page says "Something went wrong" instead of "Order placed".
reply.hypothesis: The test does what a customer does and expects the right outcome. The order request fails, so the app is broken, not the test.
reply.confidence_rationale: Every step of the test succeeded; only the outcome differs, and the page itself reports an error.
reasoning_steps: The email was filled in and the Place order button was clicked without errors.
The status then reads "Something went wrong. Please try again."
That is an error message from the app, not a changed label or a slow page.
Changing the assertion would hide a broken checkout, so the test should stay as it is.
root_cause_evidence: status "Something went wrong. Please try again." in the page snapshot at the failure

action_taken.description: No change: the test is right and the checkout is broken.
